issues.description: The solution adds an 'age' attribute to Animal and defines constructors taking (String name, int age) for Animal and all concrete animals, but the problem statement's UML and the template Main examples treat Animal as having only a 'name' and show creating animals with a single String argument (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This constructor/attribute mismatch will confuse students about the expected constructor signature and required attributes and will prevent them from compiling/running the provided Main examples or matching tests that expect single-argument constructors.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the design consistent: either remove the 'age' attribute from the solution and change Animal and concrete animal constructors to accept a single String name (matching the UML and Main examples), or update the problem statement and template examples to specify that Animal has an 'age' attribute and that Animal/Seal/Pig/Goat constructors accept (String name, int age). Update all examples and UML accordingly so constructor signatures and attributes match across problem, template, and solution.
